sentences.text: Yunnanolepis possessed a body shape very similar to its relative Bothriolepis and likely shared a comparable size.
The genus Yunnanolepis was first described by Liu in 1963.

Fossils of this species are found in Early to Middle Devonian rock layers in Southern China, specifically within the Xishancun, Lianhuashan, and Xitun Formations, and also in Middle Devonian strata in Vietnam.
Currently, the Paleobiology Database records eleven occurrences of Yunnanolepis fossils.
This animal lived during the Early to Middle Devonian periods, specifically between 419.62 and 410.62 million years ago, spanning the Lochkovian to Pragian stages.
